attempts.summary: Published node2's port-8080 app through node1 to node3 via VyOS DNAT, without exposing the rest of the private node1-node2 link. Set up a dedicated private link (eth1 on node1 10.50.50.254/24 <-> enp8s0 on node2 10.50.50.11/24), bound the app on node2 exclusively to the private IP, added a VyOS destination-NAT rule (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.11:8080) plus a default-drop forward filter with only that flow (and established/related) allowed, and fixed an asymmetric-routing issue on node2 with a policy route (packets sourced from 10.50.50.11 exit via node1 regardless of destination). Verified node3 can reach the app only through node1:8080, and cannot reach the private subnet directly (ping, direct IP:8080, or node2's shared-IP:8080 all fail). Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines, rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time, confirmed changed boot_id on each, and re-verified full functionality (NAT/firewall rules, app service, policy route, and end-to-end curl) after each restart.
